headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill mandates Dominion Energy Virginia to propose allocating certain grid infrastructure costs to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs
news_summary: This article discusses HB 1393, which, if passed, would significantly increase energy costs for data centers (roughly 16%) while decreasing costs for residential and non-high usage customers (from 3.5% to 3%). It highlights the bill's intent to shift the burden of increased generating capacity costs to high-demand users like data centers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, Virginia DEQ.
news_headline: Publicizing water use: Bills on data center water usage
news_summary: This article discusses SB 553, which requires water authorities providing water to data centers to regularly disclose the total volume withdrawn to the State Water Control Board. It highlights that the legislation aims to provide better information for informed decisions about water resources, especially given the significant water usage by data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data centers, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: What It Does
news_summary: This article details HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, requiring developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise and utilities to disclose substation information. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, empowering local governments to make informed decisions within community plans.
